title: The bread girl
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: Every morning at half past four, nineteen-year-old Thao rides her bike from her flat in Hue to a bakery near the river. By six o'clock, she has put eighty loaves of bread into two big baskets, and she starts her journey around the city.

"People think I love early mornings," Thao says, "but I hate getting up! I do it because I'm saving money. One day I want to open a small cafe with my sister." Her first customers are the workers at a hotel near the market, who buy bread for the guests' breakfast. Later, she sells to old people walking by the river.

Thao didn't plan to work for a bakery. She studied to be a nurse, and she was waiting for an answer from a hospital. Then her neighbour, who owns the bakery, broke his leg and asked her to help for two weeks. That was eight months ago.

The hardest part of the job is not the rain. "I put plastic bags over the bread, and I don't mind getting wet," she laughs. "The problem is the traffic. Some drivers don't see bikes." Next year, the bakery is going to buy her an electric bike, and she can't wait.

items.q: Why does Thao do this job?

opts.t: She wants to start her own business.
She needs money for her nursing studies.

ev.s: One day I want to open a small cafe with my sister.

items.why: Thao để dành tiền để mở quán cà phê với chị gái.

wrong.B: Thao nói cô ghét dậy sớm.
wrong.C: Cô đã học xong y tá; tiền để dành là để mở quán.

items.q: Who buys bread from Thao first?

ev.s: Her first customers are the workers at a hotel near the market

items.why: Khách đầu tiên là nhân viên một khách sạn gần chợ.

wrong.A: Người già bên sông là khách sau đó.
wrong.C: Chợ chỉ là chỗ khách sạn ở gần.

items.q: How did Thao get the job?

opts.t: Her sister works at the bakery.
The hospital had no jobs for her.

ev.s: broke his leg and asked her to help for two weeks

items.why: Ông hàng xóm chủ tiệm gãy chân và nhờ cô giúp.

wrong.A: Chị gái là người cô muốn cùng mở quán, không làm ở tiệm bánh.
wrong.C: Cô đang chờ bệnh viện trả lời; bài không nói bệnh viện hết việc.

items.q: What does Thao find hardest about the job?

ev.s: The problem is the traffic.

wrong.A: Cô nói khó nhất không phải mưa.
wrong.B: Cô ghét dậy sớm, nhưng khi nói về điều khó nhất của công việc cô nói về giao thông.

items.q: How does Thao feel about the electric bike?

opts.t: She is looking forward to it.
She is worried it will be too heavy.

ev.s: she can't wait

items.why: Cô nóng lòng chờ có xe ("can't wait").

wrong.B: Cô không nhắc ô tô.
wrong.C: Cô không nói lo xe nặng.

title: A library on the water
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: In a small fishing village in the south of Vietnam, the children have a new library. It isn't in a building. It is on an old boat. Every Saturday, the boat goes along the river and stops at four villages. Children climb on, sit on cushions and read for an hour.

The idea came from Mr Binh, a retired teacher. "Parents here are busy, but they would take their children to a library if they could," he explains. "The nearest town library is thirty kilometres away, and the bus only goes there twice a week."

At first, Mr Binh wanted to buy a small bus. He had enough money, and the roads are good now. But then a fisherman offered him his old boat for free. Students from a university in Can Tho wanted to paint it, but the children did it themselves, with help from their teachers.

The library has about six hundred books now. Most of them came from people in the city, and Mr Binh says he doesn't need any more. The children's favourites are the comics that a local artist made for them. Some people want a library building in the village. "Maybe later," he says. "First, I want a second boat for the villages further up the river."

items.q: How often does the boat visit the villages?

ev.s: Every Saturday, the boat goes along the river

items.why: Thuyền đi mỗi thứ Bảy.

wrong.A: Hai lần một tuần là số chuyến xe buýt lên thị trấn.
wrong.B: Bài nói mỗi thứ Bảy.

items.q: Why don't the children go to the town library?

opts.t: The bus doesn't go there often.

ev.s: the bus only goes there twice a week

wrong.A: Ông Bình nói bố mẹ bận nhưng sẽ đưa con đi nếu đi được.
wrong.C: Bài không nói giờ mở cửa.

items.q: Why didn't Mr Binh buy a bus?

ev.s: a fisherman offered him his old boat for free

items.why: Một ngư dân tặng ông chiếc thuyền cũ.

wrong.A: Đường bây giờ tốt.
wrong.B: Ông có đủ tiền.

items.q: Who painted the boat?

ev.s: the children did it themselves

wrong.B: Sinh viên muốn sơn nhưng trẻ em tự làm.
wrong.C: Hoạ sĩ địa phương vẽ truyện tranh.

items.q: What does Mr Binh want to do next?

opts.t: build a library in the village
find more books for the boat

ev.s: First, I want a second boat

wrong.A: Có người muốn xây thư viện, nhưng ông chỉ nói "Maybe later".
wrong.B: Ông nói không cần thêm sách.

title: The family band
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: Most weekends, the Tran family plays music at weddings and parties in Hai Phong. Dad plays the guitar, Mum sings, and their two children, Kiet and Mi, play the drums and the piano. "People think Dad started the band," says Mi, who is sixteen. "But it was my grandmother's idea. She loved music, and she paid for our first lessons."

The band started five years ago at Kiet's school concert. Now they play about four times a month. In the rainy season they don't play every weekend, because there are fewer weddings. The money helps with the children's school costs, but most of it goes on new instruments.
The hardest thing for the band isn't playing the music. "It's moving everything," Kiet laughs. "Mi's piano is really heavy, and we don't have a car. We borrow our neighbour's van."

Next year, Kiet is going to university in Hanoi. His parents hope to find a new drummer, but Mi wants to try something different. "I'd like us to play in cafes," she says. "Weddings are fun, but people don't really listen."

items.q: Whose idea was the band?

ev.s: it was my grandmother's idea

wrong.B: Bài không nhắc giáo viên âm nhạc.
wrong.C: Mọi người nghĩ là bố, nhưng không phải.

items.q: How often does the band play now?

ev.s: Now they play about four times a month.

wrong.C: Bốn lần một tháng, không phải hai.

ev.s: most of it goes on new instruments

wrong.A: Gia đình không có ô tô, mượn xe của hàng xóm.
wrong.B: Tiền chỉ giúp một phần học phí.

wrong.C: Kiệt nói khó nhất không phải âm nhạc.

ev.s: I'd like us to play in cafes

wrong.A: Kiệt mới là người ra Hà Nội học.

title: Back to school at sixty-eight
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: When Mrs Lien retired from her job at a bank, she decided to learn English. Now she is sixty-eight and goes to an evening class twice a week with twenty students. Most of them are in their twenties. "At first they called me 'Grandma', and I didn't like it," she says. "Now they just call me Lien."

Mrs Lien's son lives in Australia with his wife, who is Australian. "My grandchildren speak Vietnamese very well," she says. "But I want to have a real conversation with my son's wife. Last time we only smiled at each other!"

Many people find listening difficult, but not Mrs Lien. She watches English films every evening. "Writing is the hardest part," she says. "English spelling is crazy!" Her teacher, Mr Dung, says her speaking is the best in the class.

Next year, Mrs Lien and her husband will fly to Australia again. Last time they stayed for one month. Their son wants them to stay for a year, but this time they will only stay for two weeks. "We have a garden to look after at home," she explains.

items.q: Who are most of the other students?

ev.s: Most of them are in their twenties.

wrong.C: Các cháu đã nói tiếng Việt rất tốt.

ev.s: Writing is the hardest part

title: The kite festival
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: Every summer, the small town of Phu Minh holds a kite festival on the beach. This year, more than three hundred people took part. Many visitors think the town's fishermen started the festival, but it began twelve years ago with a primary school teacher who wanted her students to play outside more. Now it brings lots of tourists to the town.

There are three prizes: the biggest kite, the most beautiful kite and the kite that stays in the sky the longest. This year, the prize for the most beautiful kite went to Mai, aged eleven. Her kite looked like a big green dragon. "My grandmother made the frame and my dad chose the colours," she says. "I did all the painting."

The winner of the longest flight was a surprise. Everyone expected one of the big kites to win, but Mr Tuan, seventy-five, kept his small red kite in the air for over three hours. It was his tenth festival, but his first prize.

The festival is free, but visitors can buy food from local families. Last year, the money paid for the town's new swimming pool. This year it will help to repair the roof of the old primary school. The organisers want people from other countries to come, and they plan to make a website, but first they are building a car park near the beach.

items.q: How did the festival begin?

opts.t: Fishermen made kites in bad weather.
A teacher wanted children to be outside more.

ev.s: it began twelve years ago with a primary school teacher

ev.s: Everyone expected one of the big kites to win

title: A garden on the roof
instr: Read the article. For each question, choose the correct answer.
paras: Two years ago, the roof of Le Loi Secondary School in Da Nang was just an empty space. Today, it is a garden with tomatoes, beans and herbs. The school kitchen wanted to use the vegetables, but there weren't enough for six hundred students. So every week, a different class takes them home. Some parents offered to buy them, but the school said no.

The garden was the idea of a science teacher, Ms Hoa. The head teacher wasn't happy at first. "He thought the students would spend less time studying," Ms Hoa explains. An engineer checked the roof, and it was strong enough, so that was never a problem.

Each class has one day of the week in the garden. The students water the plants and take photos of them for the school website. Ms Hoa wanted them to write notes too, but there wasn't time. "I didn't like vegetables before, and I still don't," laughs Nam, aged thirteen. "But I love being outside instead of in the classroom."

Last summer, a storm broke the garden's banana tree. The students wanted to plant another banana tree, but Ms Hoa chose a lime tree, because it is smaller and safer in a storm. Now three other schools in the city want to build roof gardens.

items.q: What happens to the vegetables?

opts.t: The school sells them to parents.

ev.s: every week, a different class takes them home
